body: Split/bonus-adjusted ₹1.55 (Mar 2009) → ₹306 (Dec 2015) ≈198x; P/E 17.5 → 70 (4x) × implied EPS ~50x (from a depressed FY09 base). The run had shallow drawdowns (−32%). Early signal: the Diva opal-glass dinnerware brand (launched 2009) reached ~50% of revenue by 2014 with price increases; Sitarganj plant capacity of 8,000 tpa ran at ~85% utilisation and was doubled in late 2015; OPM 30–42%. Investors such as Ashish Kacholia held it. Ended: the stock went nowhere. ₹306 (Dec 2015) → ₹161 on 19 Nov 2026 (−48%; −70% from the 2023 ATH ₹468). Standalone sales ₹222 cr (FY15) → ₹309 cr (FY26), about 3% CAGR; EPS ~₹8. A greenfield expansion (FY22) arrived ahead of demand, with competition from Borosil and imports (narrative partly unverified). Lesson: high margins and ROCE do not equal runway. Opalware dinnerware is a small total addressable market. The rerating to 70x priced a long runway that did not exist, so check category size before extrapolating early growth.

data.early_signals: Diva brand 50% of sales; capacity at 85% utilisation
data.lesson: check TAM before paying for runway
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM); implied EPS x = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: La Opala RG 2009–2015: Diva opalware ~200x, then a decade of nothing
